question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

A lot on one’s plate

options.text: To serve all dishes on one plate

solution:
The correct answer is "**A lot to do".*****__Key Points__**Here let's see the meaning of the given idiom with an example:

__
 
• **A lot on one’s plate *(idiom) ***- A lot to do.

***Eg***. I just have a lot on my plate right now while I'm finishing up my degree and doing this huge project for work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let's here see some other related idioms:

 
• **A lot of beating - **An act of repeated hitting or striking.
 
• **A lot of good that did -** expression* Said sarcastically when something has proven utterly useless or ineffective.
